sections.label: 2035 Nationally Determined Contributions submission
sections.summary: Singapore was among 13 countries to submit 2035 NDCs on time in February 2025, pledging emissions of 45 to 50 million tonnes by 2035.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: We were among just 13 countries to submit our 2035 Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) on time in February 2025, where we pledged to reduce our emissions to between 45 and 50 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent by 2035.

sections.label: Solar capacity and electricity imports
sections.summary: Singapore reached two gigawatt-peak of installed solar capacity in 2025, raised its 2030 target to three gigawatt-peak, and awarded around 8.4 gigawatts of conditional approvals for low-carbon electricity imports.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: We are accelerating our energy transition and have achieved two gigawatt-peak of installed solar capacity in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: We have raised our 2030 solar deployment target to three gigawatt-peak, as announced at Budget 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: To date, we have also awarded around 8.4 gigawatts of conditional approvals for low-carbon electricity imports.

sections.label: Energy efficiency of appliances
sections.summary: Average energy efficiency of air-conditioners and refrigerators improved by 61% and 45% since 2009, giving annual energy savings of more than $560 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: For example, the average energy efficiency of air-conditioners and refrigerators has improved by 61% and 45% respectively since 2009.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: This translates to annual energy savings of more than $560 million.

sections.label: Regulated goods imported for own use
sections.summary: Regulated goods imported for own use will face the same MEPS and MELS compliance requirements as those intended for supply in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Specifically, regulated goods imported for own use will be subjected to similar MEPS and MELS compliance requirements as those intended for supply in Singapore.

sections.label: Enforcement on non-compliant imported goods
sections.summary: Singapore will prioritise regulating more energy intensive goods, enforce from 1 July 2026, and fine non-compliant end users up to $10,000 per import.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: We will prioritise regulating the import of more energy intensive goods, such as commercial storage refrigerators for own use, compared to less energy intensive goods, such as lamps.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: We intend to effect the enforcement regime from 1 July 2026 to deter end users from importing non-compliant regulated goods for own use and ensure compliance to the new requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: End users who import regulated goods that do not comply with MEPS and MELS requirements will face penalties of up to $10,000 in fines per import.

sections.label: Energy Efficiency Grant for SMEs
sections.summary: SMEs in food services and manufacturing meeting criteria such as 30% local shareholding can tap Enterprise Singapore's Energy Efficiency Grant, expanded to all sectors and extended to 31 March 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: For example, small and medium-sized enterprises in the food services and manufacturing sectors that meet prescribed criteria, such as the 30% local shareholding, can tap Enterprise Singapore's Energy Efficiency Grant, which has been expanded to all sectors and extended for one more year to 31 March 2028, as announced by the Senior Minister of State for Finance.

sections.label: MEPS and MELS import gap
sections.summary: MEPS and MELS for local supply of regulated goods began in 2012, but the Act did not cover goods imported by end users for own use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The MEPS and MELS for local supply of regulated goods were first introduced back in 2012.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: However, there was a gap as the Act did not cover regulated goods imported by end users for own use.

sections.label: End user import registration duties
sections.summary: End users must register imported regulated goods with NEA and show compliance with MEPS and MELS, and NEA can enforce against non-compliant importers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Despite the poorer efficiency and lifespan, many food business owners would still rather take advantage of the substantial upfront cost savings by importing these electrical appliances directly from the OEMs and wholesalers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: It will place the onus on end users, to register the imported regulated goods with NEA and demonstrate evidence of compliance with the MEPS and MELS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: NEA will also be empowered to take enforcement action against businesses and households that import non-compliant regulated goods for own use.

sections.label: F&B appliance numbers and energy
sections.summary: The question asks whether NEA estimates the total electrical appliances procured annually and their total annual energy consumption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Given the large number of F&B businesses, coupled with the short average lifespan of two to three years for refrigerators, chillers and freezers, does NEA have an estimate of the total number of electrical appliances and equipment that may be procured annually, as well as the total annual energy consumption?

sections.label: Digital enforcement and local SMEs
sections.summary: The question asks how the Ministry will ensure digital enforcement powers do not unfairly penalise local SMEs, and whether there will be a grace period or simplified verification pathway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: How will the Ministry ensure that these digital enforcement powers do not unfairly penalise local SMEs, who may inevitably fall victim to automated take-down algorithms?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Will there be a grace period or a simplified verification pathway for local micro-enterprises to ensure they are not crowded out of the digital marketplace by larger players with deeper pockets for compliance?

sections.label: Software degradation and integrity requirements
sections.summary: The questions ask how NEA will monitor software driven energy degradation after registration, and whether manufacturers must declare paid subscriptions needed to maintain MEPS ratings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Two, how does the NEA intend to monitor and regulate software driven energy degradation once an item has been registered and cleared for use?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Three, will the Government consider a software integrity requirement where manufacturers must declare if their hardware requires a paid subscription to maintain its registered MEPS rating?

sections.label: Regulations and 2030 emissions target
sections.summary: The question asks how these regulations will contribute to the national target of peaking emissions at 60,000 kilotonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Specifically, how will these regulations contribute to our national target of peaking emissions at 60,000 kilotonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2030?

sections.label: Top-ups for lower-income families
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry will consider top-ups to the Climate Friendly Households Programme or other social equity measures for lower-income families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider top-ups to the Climate Friendly Households Programme or other social equity measures to ensure lower-income families are not priced out of the appliance market by these stricter import controls?

sections.label: Excluding lighting from import regulations
sections.summary: Asks for the specific data driven justification for excluding lighting from own-use import regulations at this stage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: What is the specific data driven justification for excluding lighting from own-use import regulations at this stage?

sections.label: Aggregate energy reduction update
sections.summary: Asks the Senior Minister of State for an update on aggregate energy reduction achieved to date under the MEPS regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The 2024 amendments mandated the MEPS, which are more prescriptive regarding actual performance levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: So, can I ask the Senior Minister of State to provide an update, for facilities under this regime for over the last decade, what is the actual aggregate energy reduction achieved to date?

sections.label: Regulating hidden energy wastage, CFHP subsidies
sections.summary: Calls for regulating hidden energy wastage and increasing CFHP subsidies so vulnerable groups are not excluded, while supporting the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Government must regulate this "hidden" energy wastage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Restricting online purchases of cheap electrical appliances may increase living costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Government should increase subsidies under the Climate Friendly Households Programme (CFHP) to ensure vulnerable groups are not excluded because they cannot afford expensive energy-efficient appliances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, whilst I have the above concerns, I still support this Bill.

sections.label: Support for Energy Conservation Amendment Bill
sections.summary: Supports the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill, saying it closes a gap by regulating goods accessed through global procurement channels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I rise in support of the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This amendment comes at a time of volatility in global energy markets and where energy efficiency remains one of our first lines of defence against rising fuel costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I support the Bill because it closes a gap in our energy efficiency framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: While regulating local supply has been effective, global procurement channels now allow individuals and SMEs to access non-compliant goods directly.

sections.label: Share of regulated goods entering Singapore
sections.summary: Asks the Senior Minister of State for the Government's assessment of the percentage of regulated goods entering Singapore outside MEPS and MELS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Could the Senior Minister of State share the Government's assessment of the percentage of regulated goods currently entering Singapore, through direct imports or other channels, that may previously have fallen outside of the MEPS and MELS frameworks?

sections.label: Air-conditioner online versus local price
sections.summary: An approved single-phase air-conditioner costs about $3,299 online and $3,999 bought locally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Importing an approved single-phase air-conditioning costs about $3,299 online, while it costs $3,999 when bought locally.

sections.label: NEA supplier registration fees and time
sections.summary: NEA's website shows new supplier registration takes seven working days, with a Variable Refrigerant Flow air-conditioner fee of $85 and $55 yearly renewal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A simple search on NEA's website shows that for new registrants to be a supplier of regulated goods, the application takes seven working days, and for a Variable Refrigerant Flow air-conditioner a new registration fee costs $85 with renewal fees of $55 yearly.

sections.label: SME import lead time and compliance cost
sections.summary: The member asks whether NEA assessed average lead time and total compliance cost for SMEs importing regulated goods for their own use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In that case, the amendment may not achieve its intended deterrent effects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, I would ask the Ministry whether NEA has assessed the average lead time and total compliance cost for SMEs importing regulated goods for their own use.

sections.label: Expanding Energy Efficiency Grant scope
sections.summary: The member encourages the Ministry to consider expanding the Energy Efficiency Grant's scope to cover all regulated goods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I note that Senior Minister of State, Finance, has already expanded this Energy Efficiency Grant to all sectors today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I would encourage the Ministry to consider further expanding Energy Efficiency Grant's scope to cover all regulated goods.

sections.label: Supporting Bill and SME compliance
sections.summary: The member supports the Bill, which aligns imported electronic goods with energy efficiency standards and labelling requirements already applied to commercially supplied goods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government and the people must work hand-in-hand in order to ensure that not only our climate targets and energy goals are met, but our economy continues to grow on a model of sustainable energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: With this in mind, I support the Bill and look forward to the Senior Minister of State's clarifications, particularly on how we can ensure that SMEs are supported to comply, even as we strengthen our energy resilience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Extending our energy efficiency framework to cover goods imported for personal use is a logical and necessary step.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This Bill will align all imported electronic goods with the energy efficiency standards and labelling requirements that already applied to goods supplied commercially in Singapore, ensuring a level playing field and giving consumers a consistent basis for informed purchasing decisions.

sections.label: Leveraging trade information certificate framework
sections.summary: The member asks whether the Ministry will consider leveraging the trade information certificate framework under the Regulation of Imports and Exports Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, rather than building a new declaration regime from scratch, will the Ministry consider leveraging the trade information certificate framework under the regulation of Imports and Exports Act?

sections.label: Director-General imposing registration conditions
sections.summary: The Director-General may impose, modify or revoke conditions of a registration at any time after registration or renewal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Under the new sections 13(2A) and 15(5), the Director-General may, at any time after registration or renewal, impose new conditions on or modify or revoke existing conditions of a registration.

sections.label: Energy Conservation Act joint administration
sections.summary: The Energy Conservation Act is jointly administered by MSE and MOT, with border enforcement requiring cooperation from Singapore Customs, ICA and possibly IMDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Energy Conservation Act is jointly administered by MSE, which oversees the industry and household sectors, and MOT, which oversees the transport sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Enforcement at the border will require the active cooperation of Singapore Customs for commercial and postal shipments, the ICA for goods brought in at the land and air checkpoints and potentially, the Info-communications Media Development Authority for enforcement against online platforms and digital advertisements.

sections.label: Assurance on coordination and resources
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Senior Minister of State to assure the Chamber of a clear interagency coordination framework and adequate NEA resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Such matters are typically handled through administrative arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But given the breadth of the new regime, I would ask the Senior Minister of State to assure this Chamber that, first, there is a clear interagency coordination framework between MSE and MOT, as well as between NEA and other enforcement agencies with defined roles and responsibilities for each agency involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, that NEA will have adequate resources, both in terms of manpower and technical capabilities to administer the new registration, inspection and waiver processes for personal imports, which will be a significant expansion of its current workload.

sections.label: Single point of contact for importers
sections.summary: The speaker asks for a single point of contact or one-stop service so importers are not shuttled between agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Third, there will be a single point of contact on one stop service for importers, so that individuals and businesses are not shuttled between MSE, MOT, NEA, Singapore Customs and ICA, when trying to comply with the new requirements.

sections.label: Bill extends regime to personal imports
sections.summary: The Bill extends the regime to regulated goods imported by end users for their own use and gives stronger tools against non-compliant advertisements.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill now takes the next step in this journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It closes an increasingly important gap by extending the regime to regulated goods imported by end users for their own use, and it also gives the Government stronger tools to deal with non-compliant advertisement of regulated goods that are accessible in Singapore, including the online space.

sections.label: Clarifying compliance cost implications
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Ministry publicly clarify compliance costs, including waivers for end users and the $80 per model cost for local suppliers.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Related to this, it might be helpful if the Ministry can also publicly clarify upfront the compliance cost implication, for instance, the waiving of cost for end users and $80 cost per model of regulated goods applied to local suppliers.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I note that the Bill also extends waiver mechanism to persons who intends to import for his or her own use and is unable to comply with a requirement in a particular case, which is reflected in a proposed amendment to section 31B.

sections.label: In-person registration option
sections.summary: Asks whether people who are not digitally confident can register in person.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Would there be a possibility that they can register in person simply because they are not digitally confident?

sections.label: Mandatory energy labelling scheme
sections.summary: Raises the mandatory energy labelling scheme, the sticker seen on fridges bought from Best Denki.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: My third point is on the mandatory energy labelling scheme or easily known as the sticker that you see on the fridge that you need to buy from Best Denki.

sections.label: Online advertising provision
sections.summary: Asks about a transition period for platforms and whether the framework extends to peer-to-peer market spaces like Carousell.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: My last point is about online advertising provision.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I understand the need for stronger powers in this space as purchaser shifts online, it will make little sense to just only tighten offline while leaving major loopholes in the digital market space.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, will there be a transition period for platforms to review and update their listing?

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Will the framework focus mainly on largely e-commerce operators or could it also extend to peer-to-peer market spaces, like Carousell, where individual users upload listings directly.

sections.label: Bill targets party making supply
sections.summary: States the Bill targets the party making the prohibited supply instead of only traditional suppliers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Instead of focusing only on traditional suppliers, the Bill targets the party making the prohibited supply and this matters.

sections.label: Support for smaller firms
sections.summary: Asks whether there will be more targeted support, transitional assistance or differentiated timelines for smaller firms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry elaborate on whether there will be more targeted support, transitional assistance, or differentiated timelines beyond the current scheme for smaller firms?

sections.label: Clause 7 flexibility
sections.summary: States that clause 7 gives flexibility, but flexibility can also create uncertainty.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Yes, clause 7 gives flexibility, but flexibility can also create uncertainty.

sections.label: Direct imports under 10%
sections.summary: The Bill addresses direct imports, currently estimated at less than 10%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The Bill addresses direct imports, currently estimated at less than 10%.

sections.label: Support for Energy Conservation Bill
sections.summary: A Member states in Mandarin support for the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   I support the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill 2026.

sections.label: Core purpose of Bill
sections.summary: The Bill's core purpose is that all relevant equipment, for sale or own use, must meet energy efficiency standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Simply put, the core purpose of this Bill is to ensure that all relevant equipment, whether for sale or imported by businesses for their own use, must comply with energy efficiency standards.

sections.label: Same standards for all equipment
sections.summary: The amendment requires equipment for sale or own use, if regulated, to comply with the same energy efficiency standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Through this amendment, regardless of whether equipment is for sale or own use, as long as it falls under regulated products, it must comply with the same energy efficiency standards.

sections.label: Compliance checks and market fairness
sections.summary: A Member asks how Government will ensure compliance, suggesting stronger spot checks and independent assessment mechanisms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Since this Bill expands the regulatory scope of regulated products, may I ask the Minister how the Government will ensure enterprises truly comply with these requirements when importing and using relevant equipment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the long run, this not only undermines system credibility but also affects market fairness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Therefore, I suggest the Government consider strengthening spot checks and independent assessment mechanisms to ensure energy efficiency standards can be implemented in real operations.

sections.label: Support, financing and talent
sections.summary: A Member asks about support programmes or financing, and suggests industry-higher education cooperation for energy efficiency courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The reason is not that it is unwilling to improve efficiency but that equipment updates often involve one-time investment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Therefore, may I ask the Minister whether the Government plans to further strengthen support programmes or financing mechanisms to assist businesses in adopting more efficient equipment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In other words, even if businesses purchase efficient equipment, without professional personnel to analyse energy consumption data and optimise operating methods, the equipment's efficiency may not be fully realised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Therefore, I suggest the Government strengthen cooperation between industry and higher education institutions to develop more professional courses in energy efficiency and energy management, to ensure businesses can obtain the talent they need.

sections.label: Energy Conservation Amendment Bill support
sections.summary: The Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill strengthens Singapore's energy efficiency framework by closing regulatory gaps and ensuring regulated goods meet energy efficiency standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For these reasons, I support this Bill. : Mr Deputy Speaker, the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill strengthens Singapore's energy efficiency framework by closing regulatory gaps and ensuring that regulated goods, whether supplied in the market or imported for own use, meet the required energy efficiency standards.

sections.label: Electricity consumption greenhouse gas emissions
sections.summary: Around 40% of Singapore's greenhouse gas emissions are linked to electricity consumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Around 40% of Singapore's greenhouse gas emissions are linked to electricity consumption.

sections.label: Extension to own-use imports
sections.summary: The amendment extends these requirements to goods imported for a person's own use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The amendment now extends these requirements to goods imported for a person's own use.

sections.label: Importer registration of regulated goods
sections.summary: Each importer must register regulated goods, even if another importer already registered the same product.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Under the proposed framework, each importer is required to register regulated goods, even if the same product has already been registered by another importer.

sections.label: Consumer education and online labelling
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government will strengthen consumer education and require clear energy efficiency labelling on online marketplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider strengthening consumer education and requiring clear visibility of energy efficiency labelling on online marketplaces, for example, by mandating the display of Singapore energy labels in listings?

sections.label: Own-use import registration requirements
sections.summary: Regulated goods imported for own use must be registered with NEA, meet MEPS requirements and be affixed with an energy label where applicable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Under the proposed amendments, regulated goods imported for own use must be registered with NEA, meet MEPS requirements based on prescribed tests and, where applicable, be affixed with an energy label.

sections.label: Simplified processes for SMEs
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether simplified or streamlined processes will be available for SMEs and for those importing goods in small volumes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: In particular, I would like to ask whether simplified or streamlined processes will be made available for SMEs as well as for individuals or businesses importing goods in small volumes.

sections.label: Obligations on platform operators
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to consider placing clear obligations on platform operators to prevent listing of non-compliant products.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Given the significant presence of e-commerce in our daily lives, enforcement cannot rely solely on downstream checks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to consider placing clear obligations on platform operators to prevent the listing of non-compliant products in the first place.

sections.label: Support for energy-efficient appliances
sections.summary: The Government could consider targeted support measures such as rebates, grants or co-funding schemes to defray upfront costs and make energy-efficient appliances more accessible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: To address this, the Government could consider targeted support measures, increase targeted support measures, such as rebates, grants or co-funding schemes to help defray upfront costs and make energy-efficient appliances more accessible.

sections.label: Bill's intent and public awareness
sections.summary: A more comprehensive and consistent approach can enhance public awareness, and the Bill reinforces Singapore's commitment to sustainability while safeguarding energy security.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: With a more comprehensive and consistent approach, the level of public awareness can be enhanced. : Mr Deputy Speaker, the intention behind this Bill is sound and forward-looking.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: It reinforces Singapore's commitment to sustainability while safeguarding our energy security.

sections.label: MEPS and MELS coverage gap
sections.summary: MEPS and MELS apply only to local suppliers, leaving goods imported directly for one's own use unregulated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Today, our Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS) and Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme (MELS) apply only to local suppliers, leaving goods imported directly for one's own use unregulated.

sections.label: Commercial refrigerator lifecycle costs
sections.summary: A commercial refrigerator can have lifecycle costs about 30% lower than a non-compliant one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A commercial refrigerator can have lifecycle costs about 30% lower than a non-compliant one.

sections.label: Cost impact on households and SMEs
sections.summary: Asks what the projected cost impact on households and SMEs will be when the amendments take effect if direct imports are currently under 10%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If direct imports are currently less than 10%, what is the projected cost impact on households and SMEs when these amendments take effect?

sections.label: Three months for households and SMEs
sections.summary: States that three months may not be sufficient for households renovating, SMEs procuring, or businesses with goods in transit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Three months may not be sufficient for households amid renovation, SMEs amid procurement, or businesses with goods already in transit.

sections.label: Energy conservation and Singapore's preparation
sections.summary: States that getting this right makes energy conservation not feel like a burden and that this tests how Singapore prepares for an uncertain world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Because if we get this right, energy conservation will not feel like a burden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And let us be reminded that this is not just an energy policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is a test of how we prepare Singapore for an uncertain world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Because in a world that we cannot control, the strength of Singapore will depend on what we choose to control, what we choose to conserve and what we choose to secure.

sections.label: Clause 7 importer registration requirement
sections.summary: Clause 7 amends the Energy Conservation Act to require an importer of regulated goods for their own use to register them even if another importer already registered them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Clause 7 of the Bill amends the Energy Conservation Act to require an importer of regulated goods for their own use to register the regulated good(s), “even if another importer has already so registered such regulated good(s)”.

sections.label: Clause 12 free samples requirement
sections.summary: Clause 12 lets the Director-General require an individual importer of regulated goods for their own use to provide free samples and documents, which may be challenging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Next, clause 12 of the Bill amends the Energy Conservation Act such that the Director-General may require an individual importer of regulated goods for their own use to provide free of charge samples to the Director-General for the purpose of testing or analysis, and any other document that the Director-General requires.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is quite likely that for importers who are importing for their own use to only import one piece of the good, so it could perhaps, be challenging for them to provide “free of charge” samples to the Director-General for the purpose of testing and analysis.

sections.label: ELS Portal registration and fees
sections.summary: States the ELS Portal registration relies on Corppass for businesses and companies, and registration fees range from $70 to $85 by regulated goods type.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For example, the current Energy Labelling Scheme (ELS) Portal for registration relies on Corppass, which are for businesses and companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Second, the application for the registration of regulated goods involves fees that are chargeable between $70 and $85, depending on the type of regulated goods.

sections.label: Energy Conservation Amendment Bill level playing field
sections.summary: The Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill is introduced to ensure a level playing field for users and suppliers of regulated goods and improve Singapore's energy efficiency.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We have also noticed that some businesses are also directly importing regulated goods, such as commercial storage refrigerators, for their own use.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: And so, that is part of the need to introduce the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill to ensure a level playing field for both users and suppliers of regulated goods in Singapore, many of which are SMEs, and which are already complying with the Energy Conservation Act and for us to also improve our overall energy efficiency in Singapore.

sections.label: Lights excluded from Bill
sections.summary: Lights are excluded from the Bill because regulating them would impose a disproportionate compliance burden on end users such as households.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: For example, we have excluded lights from the Bill because regulating them will impose a disproportionate compliance burden on end users, such as households that occasionally import a few lights.

sections.label: Registration fees waived for end users
sections.summary: Registration and renewal fees will be waived for end users who import regulated goods for their own use.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We have taken in the feedback to reduce the compliance burden on end users who are importing regulated goods for their own use, and they typically cannot spread the registration costs across multiple units.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: So, therefore, the registration and renewal fees on end users who import regulated goods for their own use will be waived.

sections.label: NEA upgrading ELS Portal
sections.summary: NEA will upgrade the ELS Portal for a better user experience for those applying to register their appliance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: NEA will upgrade the ELS Portal for a better user experience for those applying to register their appliance.

sections.label: Minister empowered over online platforms
sections.summary: The proposed amendments will empower the Minister to make regulations compelling online platforms in Singapore to remove or rectify listings of non-compliant regulated goods.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments will empower the Minister to make regulations to compel online platforms in Singapore to remove or rectify listings of non-compliant listings of regulated goods.

sections.label: New regulations scope own use
sections.summary: The new regulations will only apply to new regulated goods imported into Singapore for the purposes of own use.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The new regulations will only apply to new regulated goods imported into Singapore, for the purposes of own use.

sections.label: NEA enforcement and regulation start date
sections.summary: NEA will conduct surveillance and investigations to enforce compliance, with new regulations intended from 1 July 2026 for platform operators to adjust.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: NEA will conduct surveillance and investigations to enforce compliance as required.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We intend to effect the new regulations from 1 July 2026 to give platform operators time to adjust to the new regulations.

sections.label: Per-import penalties for non-compliant goods
sections.summary: Penalties are imposed per import, with fines up to $10,000 per import of non-compliant goods for own use.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Penalties will be imposed on a per-import basis, with fines of up to $10,000 per import of non-compliant goods for own use.

sections.label: Per-import penalty framework consistency
sections.summary: A per-import penalty framework is consistent with similar legislation, including the Environmental Protection and Management Act 1999, which fines up to $10,000 per contravening supply or import.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: A penalty framework on a per-import basis is also consistent with penalty regimes in similar legislation, including the Environmental Protection and Management Act 1999, which imposes a fine not exceeding $10,000 for each contravening supply or import of non-compliant greenhouse gas goods, such as commercial chillers.

sections.label: Energy Efficiency Grant expansion and extension
sections.summary: The Energy Efficiency Grant base tier has been expanded to all sectors and support extended to 31 March 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As announced by the Senior Minister of State for Finance, the Energy Efficiency Grant base tier has been expanded to all sectors and support will be extended for another year, to 31 March 2028.

sections.label: Climate Vouchers for eligible households
sections.summary: The Government has provided eligible households with $400 of Climate Vouchers in total over the last two Budgets under the enhanced Climate Friendly Households Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: For households, the Government has provided eligible households with $400 of Climate Vouchers in total over the last two Budgets, under the enhanced Climate Friendly Households Programme.

sections.label: Life-cycle costs of compliant refrigerators
sections.summary: Life-cycle costs of MEPS-compliant commercial storage refrigerators are on average 30% lower than non-compliant models.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: For example, life-cycle costs of MEPS-compliant commercial storage refrigerators are on average 30% lower than non-compliant models.

sections.label: Future energy savings estimate
sections.summary: At a future time, total estimated annual consumption could be assessed, with an estimated 30% cost reduction over the life-cycle of a compliant good versus a non-compliant good.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, at a future time, we should be in a better position then to think about what is the total estimated annual consumption to include what, today, would have regulated and unregulated goods.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And so, the reduction in energy savings, we can make an estimate, and we have estimated that there is about a 30% reduction in costs and over a life-cycle of the compliant good compared to a non-compliant good.

sections.label: Businesses use compliant suppliers
sections.summary: Most businesses involved today already engage with MEPS- and MELS-compliant suppliers and purchase from them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Today, most of the businesses involved are already engaged with MEPS- and MELS-compliant suppliers and are already involved with purchasing from the suppliers.

sections.label: Director-General and NEA measures
sections.summary: The Act provides for the Director-General and NEA to exercise a range of measures for goods that are non-compliant or become non-compliant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The Act provides for the Director-General and NEA to exercise a range of measures should they come across a good, which is non-compliant or which was declared to be compliant and is now subsequently non-compliant.

sections.label: Action against importer or manufacturer
sections.summary: Action could potentially be taken against both the importer and the manufacturer, with higher scrutiny where deliberate conduct is known.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Whether the action would be taken against the person who imported or the manufacturer, the answer is potentially both, because now that you know that this business or this person may have deliberately done it, we would have a higher level of scrutiny.
